# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_CONTRACTION_EXPANSION_REVERSAL

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon (EMA_9 − EMA_50) contracts tightly to <0.1×ATR(20) for ≥3 consecutive bars, a subsequent expansion where price closes outside the ribbon with elevated volume signals a reversal. This edge exists because contraction indicates low volatility and equilibrium, while expansion with volume reflects a break of that equilibrium, often leading to mean-reversion moves in choppy markets (VIX 12-22).

## Mechanism

Calculate ribbon_width = |EMA_9 − EMA_50| and ATR_20. Contraction trigger: ribbon_width < 0.1 × ATR_20 for ≥3 consecutive bars. Then seek a bar where:
- If prior trend was down (close < EMA_50 before contraction period): close > EMA_9 and volume > 1.3 × 20-bar average volume → enter long
- If prior trend was up (close ≥ EMA_50 before contraction period): close < EMA_20 and volume > 1.3 × 20-bar average volume → enter short
Exit: Initial stop at opposite ribbon edge (long stop at EMA_20, short stop at EMA_9). Target = 2R. Trail with Chandelier exit after 1R profit. Regime filter: Only trade when VIX between 12-22.
